---
title: "Many-facet Rasch measurement"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5, dpi = 110)
library(IRTistic)
set.seed(11)
```

When performances are scored by raters, the score depends on the person, the
rater's severity and the difficulty of the criterion. The many-facet Rasch
model (Linacre, 1989) puts all of these on one logit scale. IRTistic
estimates it by marginal maximum likelihood and reports it in the layout of
Linacre's FACETS program, so FACETS users will recognise every table.

```{r}
ratings <- sim_mfrm(n_person = 120, n_rater = 6, n_criterion = 4, ncat = 5, design = 0.7)
head(ratings)
mf <- mfrm_fit(ratings, person = "person", facets = c("rater", "criterion"), score = "score")
mf
```

## Measurement reports

```{r}
rep <- facet_report(mf)
irt_table(rep)
irt_table(rep, facet = "rater")
irt_table(rep, facet = "categories")
```

## The variable map

```{r, fig.height = 6}
plot(mf, "facets")
```

## Rating scale functioning and fit

```{r}
plot(mf, "categories")
plot(mf, "fit")
```

## Rater bias

```{r}
bias <- mfrm_bias(mf, c("rater", "criterion"))
irt_table(head(bias, 8))
plot_bias(bias)
```

A partial credit structure for each criterion is one argument away:

```{r}
mf_pcm <- mfrm_fit(ratings, "person", c("rater", "criterion"), "score",
                   model = "pcm", step_facet = "criterion")
anova_like <- data.frame(model = c("RSM", "PCM"), logLik = c(mf$loglik, mf_pcm$loglik),
                         AIC = c(AIC(mf), AIC(mf_pcm)), BIC = c(BIC(mf), BIC(mf_pcm)))
irt_table(anova_like)
```
